title.en: The Golden Record Cover: How to Play It
title.zh: 金唱片的封套：怎样播放它

basis.en: A work of NASA, the United States space agency, and so a US federal government work, which is not subject to copyright (17 U.S.C. § 105).
basis.zh: 美国国家航空航天局（NASA）的作品，属于美国联邦政府作品，不受版权保护（《美国法典》第 17 编第 105 条）。

note.en: The aluminium cover of each Voyager record carries the instructions for playing it, drawn rather than written, and this NASA page explains every drawing in turn. Read it as a lesson in writing for a stranger: give the unit first, then the speed, then a test picture so the reader can check their own work. One small thing to notice: this page gives the half-life of uranium-238 as 4.51 billion years, while NASA’s page on the making of the record gives the modern figure, 4.468 billion.
note.zh: 每张旅行者号唱片的铝制封套上，都画着——而不是写着——播放它的说明；NASA 的这一页把这些图逐一解释。不妨把它当作一堂课来读：怎样给一个陌生人写东西——先给出单位，再给出转速，然后附上一幅测试图，让读者自己检验。有个小地方值得留意：这一页给出的铀-238 半衰期是 45.1 亿年，而 NASA 介绍唱片制作的那一页用的是现代数值 44.68 亿年。

pick.en: I keep this one for its order of operations. Before it says anything about Earth, the cover teaches its reader how to read it, and then hands over a circle so the reader can tell whether they have it right. Much of what I do is the same task at a smaller scale: work out what a reader needs first, and give them a way to check.
pick.zh: 我留下它，是因为它安排事情的顺序。在说起地球的任何事情之前，封套先教会读者怎样读它，然后递上一个圆，让读者自己判断有没有读对。我做的许多事情，都是同一件事的小号版本：先想清楚读者首先需要什么，再给他们一个核对的办法。

excerpt.orig: The stylus is in the correct position to play the record from the beginning.
excerpt.en: The stylus is in the correct position to play the record from the beginning.
excerpt.zh: 唱针停在正确的位置上，可以从头开始播放。

marginalia.at: the time period associated with a fundamental transition of the hydrogen atom
marginalia.en: Every number on the cover is counted in this one unit, so a reader who decodes the hydrogen drawing in the lower right can read all the others. The page explains it last; in logic it comes first.
marginalia.zh: 封套上的每一个数都以这一个单位计量，所以读懂右下角那幅氢原子图的人，就能读懂其余所有的图。这一页把它放在最后才解释；按逻辑，它排在最前。

marginalia.at: A circle was used in this picture
marginalia.en: A circle shows an error at a glance: get the proportions wrong and it turns into an ellipse. The test needs no instructions of its own, which is what makes it a good test.
marginalia.zh: 圆能让错误一目了然：比例弄错了，它就变成椭圆。这个检验本身不需要任何说明，这正是它好的地方。

marginalia.at: This should be a check on the epoch of launch, which is also described by the pulsar map on the record cover.
marginalia.en: Two independent clocks, the uranium and the pulsars, are given so that each can check the other. It is the same habit as the test picture: when writing to a stranger, give two ways to be sure.
marginalia.zh: 铀和脉冲星，两只彼此独立的时钟，可以互相核对。这和那幅测试图出于同一种习惯：给陌生人写信时，给出两种确认的办法。
